mcqs.q: On average, how many words did owners report their dogs respond to?
mcqs.e: Owners reported dogs responded to ~89 words on average (78 listed plus 11 added).

mcqs.q: How many distinct word categories did the Principal Component Analysis reveal?
mcqs.e: Three types emerged: General Words, Verbs (Commands), and Nouns.

mcqs.q: Which factors uniquely predicted the number of words reported?
o: Dog work status, learning speed, and breed type
mcqs.e: No owner characteristics predicted word count; dog professional work status, learning speed, and breed type did.

mcqs.q: Most vocalizations in the unsolvable food task were directed at whom?
mcqs.e: 67.7% of vocalizations were directed at the owner rather than the food.

mcqs.q: What proportion of the dogs vocalized at all?
mcqs.e: Only 21.6% (11 of 51 dogs) vocalized during the task.

mcqs.q: Which vocalization type predominated?
mcqs.e: Barks and bark-related sounds made up 67.72% of vocalizations versus 32.27% whines.

mcqs.q: On their very first choice, dogs' preference for the larger food quantity was at what level?
mcqs.e: First-choice performance was at chance (P=0.06); above-chance preference emerged only with experience.

mcqs.q: What did the results suggest drives dogs' quantity choices?
o: Sensitivity to recent experience and outcomes
mcqs.e: Dogs adjusted behaviour based on outcomes, even after a single trial, confirming experience-sensitivity.

mcqs.q: Which factors significantly affected overall performance?
o: Owner sex and time of day
mcqs.e: Numerical comparison difficulty and neuter status significantly affected overall (but not first-choice) performance.

mcqs.q: Which personality trait was associated with LOWER owner-perceived dominance?
mcqs.e: More agreeable dogs scored lower on dominance; extroversion, conscientiousness, and openness scored higher.

mcqs.q: How did age relate to dominance?
o: Older dogs tended to be more dominant
mcqs.e: Older dogs tended to be more dominant, consistent with prior studies.

mcqs.q: How many of the Big Five personality traits showed a significant association with dominance?
mcqs.e: Four of the five traits (extroversion, conscientiousness, openness, agreeableness) were significantly associated.

mcqs.q: After up to a 12-month gap in exposure, recall of previously trained odors was:
mcqs.e: Dogs recalled odors unexposed for 12 months with 100% accuracy and no rise in false alarms.

mcqs.q: Up to how many cumulative odor discriminations were dogs trained on?
mcqs.e: Odors were trained in sets of 10 up to a cumulative total of 40 over 16 months.

mcqs.q: What effect did learning new odors have on recall of previously trained odors?
mcqs.e: Dogs showed little to no decrease in recall of prior odors when learning new ones.

mcqs.q: Which behavioral problems were ameliorated after PS128 probiotic treatment?
mcqs.e: General stability improved, with aggression and separation anxiety ameliorated after treatment.

mcqs.q: What biochemical change was seen in dogs with separation anxiety?
mcqs.e: A significant decrease in the 5-HIAA/5-HT ratio suggested a serotonin-related mechanism.

mcqs.q: Through what proposed axis does the probiotic act?
mcqs.e: Effects were attributed to neuromodulation through the gut-brain axis, with serotonin involvement.

mcqs.q: What did the survey suggest about scientific welfare research reaching industry?
o: It may not be successfully translating into practice
mcqs.e: Findings suggested published research may not be translating into evidence-based industry changes.

mcqs.q: Differences in welfare beliefs were associated with which respondent factors?
o: Kennel experience, role, age, and gender
mcqs.e: Beliefs differed by kennel facility experience, employment role, age, and gender.

mcqs.q: What dimension did authors argue future welfare assessment models should include?
mcqs.e: They concluded models should include the critical dimension of human-animal interaction.

mcqs.q: How well did cooperative care training transfer to the actual veterinary examination?
mcqs.e: Transfer of trained skills to the blinded vet examination was overall poor.

mcqs.q: How did compliance in the training group compare at the second visit?
mcqs.e: Compliance was significantly lower in the training group during the second visit (p=0.04).

mcqs.q: HR/HRV data indicated the examination, versus the waiting room, was:
mcqs.e: Higher HR and lower HRV during the exam indicated it was more stressful than the waiting room.

mcqs.q: During the COVID-19 quarantine, shelter dog activity patterns:
o: Remained at a constant average across the day
mcqs.e: Pre-COVID showed less afternoon activity; during COVID activity stayed at a constant average.

mcqs.q: The automated video analysis reached what accuracy versus manual coding?
mcqs.e: Automated active/non-active classification reached above 79% accuracy versus manual coding.

mcqs.q: What did authors conclude about the automated analysis method?
o: A perfect replacement for manual coding
mcqs.e: They concluded automated analysis can serve as a hands-off tool to monitor shelter dog activity.

mcqs.q: Across all three age timepoints, dogs were most commonly walked:
mcqs.e: At 16 weeks, 9 months, and 15 months, dogs were most commonly walked twice daily.

mcqs.q: As dogs aged from 16 weeks to 15 months, total walk duration:
mcqs.e: Total weekday and weekend walk duration increased significantly as dogs aged.

mcqs.q: As dogs aged, the proportion of walk time spent on lead:
mcqs.e: On-lead time fell from ≥75% in puppies to <25% in older dogs, a significant decrease.

mcqs.q: In which respects did the authors argue companion dogs have good welfare versus village dogs?
mcqs.e: Companion dogs were said to fare well on security, nutritional needs, and veterinary care.

mcqs.q: What nutrition-related welfare problem was specifically noted in companion dogs?
mcqs.e: Despite met nutritional needs, companion dogs have a high prevalence of obesity.

mcqs.q: What comparison group did the authors use to assess the 'petification' of dogs?
mcqs.e: They compared companion dog welfare to that of modern village dogs, resembling historic dog life.

mcqs.q: What was the effect of owner presence versus absence on dogs' stress-related behaviour during the examination phase?
mcqs.e: Owner presence had no significant effect on stress behaviour or handleability during examination (P>0.05).

mcqs.q: In the presence of their owner, dogs were:
o: More willing to enter and more relaxed during exploration
mcqs.e: With owners present, dogs were more willing to enter the room and more relaxed during exploration.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend for canine welfare during consultations?
o: Allow the owner to stay in the room
Examine dogs in the waiting room
mcqs.e: Results suggest allowing the owner to stay in the room is the better option for canine welfare.
